subject: Proposed reserved uplift conversion + invoice-anchoring option
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alec Chen <alec.chen@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed reserved uplift conversion + invoice-anchoring option

Hi Alec —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise option you can take to Procurement that should address Novacorp's need for predictable unit economics while preserving flexibility for burst:

- Convert your existing monthly retainer into a 12-month reserved uplift (reserved GPU capacity) covering baseline usage, with the ability to burst above it at pay-as-you-go rates.
- Temporary invoice-anchoring: we hold the per-token list rate for the first 4 months after signature (no retroactive increases) while you ramp traffic into the reserved pool.
- One-off uplift credit: a 5% credit applied to the first 2 invoices as a ramp concession.
- Shortfall handling: monthly reconciliation with a 60-day true-up window (we're open to discussing a softer shortfall floor for enterprise customers).

Attached: Novacorp_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with capacity bands) and Novacorp_usage_q3.csv (last quarter baseline).

If Procurement needs a longer price hold or a defined shortfall cap, let me know — we can trade duration for a smaller uplift credit or a modest tiered discount.

Suggested next steps:
1) If this looks directionally right, I'll share a one-page summary for Procurement and loop Legal for a simple amendment.
2) We can route for e-sign (DocuSign) once terms are agreed.

Open to a quick slot Thursday morning to walk Procurement through the mechanics.

Best,
Priyom
---
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: Novacorp_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, 6 pages), Novacorp_usage_q3.csv (baseline usage)

From: Alec Chen <alec.chen@novacorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed reserved uplift conversion + invoice-anchoring option

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A couple of quick notes from our side after an initial run with Procurement: 

- They like the invoice-anchoring idea but want the price hold extended to 6 months instead of 4.
- Procurement will push back on a hard true-up that creates potential large one-time bills; they asked if we can cap a monthly shortfall exposure at 20% of the invoice in the first 6 months, with an agreed remediation cadence.
- They also asked if the one-off uplift credit can be front-loaded as a single credit on month-1 rather than split across two invoices. Easier for their accounting.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) extend the anchor to 6 months if we tighten the uplift credit (e.g., 3% upfront), and (b) accept a capped shortfall exposure as described?

If that sounds workable, I can have Procurement approve a one-page term summary and move to Legal for a quick amendment.

Best,
Alec
Alec Chen
Sr. Director, Cloud Ops — Novacorp
alec.chen@novacorp.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed reserved uplift conversion + invoice-anchoring option (internal)

Priyom / Lauren —

Quick internal read and recommended trade-offs before we go back to Alec: 

1) Anchor duration vs. credit size
   - Procurement wants 6 months. We can extend to 6 months if we reduce the ramp credit to a single upfront 3% credit applied at month-1. That preserves NRR and avoids price exposure.

2) Shortfall exposure cap
   - Accept capping the first 6 months' monthly shortfall at 20% of the invoice, but require a 12-month commit and a 30% amortization of cumulative shortfalls (i.e., spread over remaining term) to avoid material accounting drag.

3) Legal redlines to expect
   - Simple amendment with a two-paragraph shortfall cap, invoice-anchor clause, and SOW schedule for reserved capacity. Legal will push for a clear definition of "baseline usage."

4) Commercial sweetener
   - Offer a one-time technical onboarding credit (professional services credit) of up to $8k to help Novacorp migrate prefixes into the reserved pool. That doesn't affect MRR and is an easier approval for Rev Ops.

If you agree I can draft a one-pager with those exact bullets and suggested clause language for Legal.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 312-555-0110

Attachments: proposed_concessions_table.xlsx (internal)

Subject: Re: Proposed reserved uplift conversion + invoice-anchoring option

Hi Alec —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We talked this through internally and can move forward on the terms Procurement requested with the following final proposal: 

- Anchor duration: 6 months price-hold on the per-token list rate after signature.
- Ramp credit: single upfront 3% credit applied to month-1 invoice.
- Shortfall exposure: monthly shortfall capped at 20% of that month's invoice for the first 6 months. Any cumulative residual shortfall will be amortized over the remaining term (spread evenly across remaining months) — this gives you predictability while protecting Redwood from a single large bill.
- Commit: 12-month reserved uplift (baseline) with standard burst rates above reserved capacity.
- Onboarding credit: one-time professional services credit up to $8,000 to support migration into the reserved pool.

I attached an updated SOW (Novacorp_SOW_v3.pdf) and a one-page term summary for Procurement. If Procurement is comfortable, I can open a DocuSign envelope (link below) for Legal to review and sign.

DocuSign (SOW+Amendment): https://www.docusign.com/novacorp/SOW-v3
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4578

Would Thursday 10am PT work for a 20-minute run-through with Procurement and Legal? If so I'll send an invite and the one-pager in advance.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this for Q4.

Best,
